title: Parameter tuples characterize germs of flat quasi-finite affine-space charts
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $X$ a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme; def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $x\in X$ a closed point [def-weil-closed-points]. Write $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for its local ring [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], $\mathfrak m$ for its maximal ideal, and identify $\kappa(x)=R/\mathfrak m$ with $k$ via the structure map [def-weil-residue-field]. The ring $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume $R$ is Cohen–Macaulay, meaning $\operatorname{depth}(R)=\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-depth; def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $d\ge0$, let $V\subseteq X$ be an open neighbourhood of $x$, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_d\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$. Define $f:V\to\mathbf A^d_k$ by these coordinates [def-sbc-affine-space], put $a_i=f_i(x)\in k$, and let $t_i=(f_i)_x-a_i\in\mathfrak m$. The following are equivalent:

(i) There is an open neighbourhood $x\in U\subseteq V$ such that $f|_U:U\to\mathbf A^d_k$ is quasi-finite and flat [pqf-def-quasifinite; def-weil-flat-morphism].

(ii) $\dim R=d$ and $\sqrt{(t_1,\ldots,t_d)R}=\mathfrak m$.

A tuple of $d$ elements in the maximal ideal of a $d$-dimensional Noetherian local ring whose generated ideal has radical the maximal ideal is called a system of parameters. Equivalently, its quotient ring is nonzero of Krull dimension zero. The neighbourhood in (i) may be chosen affine. In particular the criterion concerns any prescribed representatives $f_i$, without altering their germs or their coordinate values.
